memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: initial assessment of type 2 diabetes and benign positional vertigo.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports occasional dizziness on turning head, mild polyuria, and fatigue.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 78 kg, BMI 24.3 (overweight). Cardiovascular regular, lungs clear. Neurological: Dix-Hallpike elicits transient vertigo with nystagmus.
IMPRESSION: 1) Type 2 diabetes, uncontrolled (HbA1c pending). 2) Benign positional vertigo.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start metformin 500 mg BD, glimepiride 1 mg OD before breakfast, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD. Betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS for vertigo. Advise diet low in refined carbs, walk 30 min daily. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, worsening vertigo, hypoglycaemia symptoms, or blood in urine.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been feeling dizzy when I look up or roll over in bed, especially in the mornings. Also I notice I am thirstier than usual and need to pass urine more often.

Reason for visit: routine diabetes and vertigo check.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says dizziness less frequent, still occasional; reports improved thirst and polyuria.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/82 mmHg, weight 77.5 kg, BMI 24.1 (overweight). Lungs clear, cardiovascular regular. Neurological: Dix-Hallpike negative today.
IMPRESSION: Type 2 diabetes – HbA1c 7.8% (elevated), fasting glucose 156 mg/dL. Benign positional vertigo – improved.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue metformin, glimepiride, sitagliptin, empagliflozin. Add lifestyle reinforcement. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, worsening vertigo, hypoglycaemia, or foot ulcer.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: worsening vertigo.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports recurrent spinning sensation on lying down, lasting <1 minute, with nausea.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/84 mmHg, weight 78 kg, BMI 24.3 (overweight). Neurological: Dix-Hallpike positive on right side with torsional nystagmus.
IMPRESSION: Benign positional vertigo – exacerbation. Diabetes stable.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue diabetes meds. Increase betahistine to 24 mg BD. Prescribe meclizine 25 mg SOS max 4 times daily. Advise vestibular exercises. Return if: vertigo with headache, double vision, weakness, fever >39°C, or hearing loss.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Refer to ENT specialist for evaluation of recurrent benign positional vertigo and consideration of vestibular rehabilitation. Please assess for possible BPPV and advise on home exercises.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: ENT review: confirmed right posterior canal BPPV. Performed Epley maneuver in clinic; patient instructed on home Brandt-Daroff exercises. Advised to continue betahistine and meclizine as needed. No further intervention required. Follow-up in 3 months if symptoms recur.

Reason for visit: routine follow-up.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports vertigo resolved after exercises; occasional mild light-headedness. No polyuria, thirst improved.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 24.0 (overweight). Lungs clear, cardiovascular regular.
IMPRESSION: Type 2 diabetes – HbA1c 7.2% (improved). Benign positional vertigo – resolved.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue metformin, glimepiride, sitagliptin, empagliflozin. Maintain betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine SOS. Advise weight reduction target 70 kg. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, worsening vertigo, hypoglycaemia, or foot symptoms.
